ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: In the figure, within $\triangle ABC$, we have $AB=AC$, and $D$ is a point on $BC$ such that $CD=AD$ and $AB=BD$. What is the measure of $\angle B$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} We have AB=AC,\\
thus $\angle B=\angle C$,\\
and since CD=DA,\\
it follows that $\angle C=\angle DAC$,\\
also given BA=BD,\\
it implies $\angle BDA=\angle BAD=2\angle C=2\angle B$,\\
furthermore, since $\angle B+\angle BAD+\angle BDA=180^\circ$,\\
we conclude $5\angle B=180^\circ$,\\
hence $\angle B=\boxed{36^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows triangle ABC with B at the lower left, C at the lower right, and A above them. Segment BC is the base, D is marked on BC between B and C, and segment AD is drawn inside the triangle. Reasoning: Let x = angle B in triangle ABC. Since AB = AC, triangle ABC is isosceles, so angle C = x. Because D lies on BC, angle ACD is the same as angle ACB, so angle ACD = x. Since CD = AD, triangle ACD is isosceles, so angle DAC = angle ACD = x. Therefore angle BAC = 180° - 2x, and angle BAD = angle BAC - angle DAC = (180° - 2x) - x = 180° - 3x. Also AB = BD, so triangle ABD is isosceles, giving angle BAD = angle BDA. In triangle ABD, the angles sum to 180°: x + angle BAD + angle BDA = 180°. Thus x + 2(180° - 3x) = 180°, so x + 360° - 6x = 180°, hence 5x = 180° and x = 36°.
